title: Tenant profile matcher and quantization fallback for cost-safe defaults
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a tenant-profile matcher that selects compact batching/caching/quant presets based on historical telemetry; add a safe quantization fallback chain and a preview CLI. Non-breaking, opt-in via feature flag.
description:
Context: Tenants exhibit wide variance in request size, burstiness, and acceptable latency/cost tradeoffs. Current global presets are either too conservative (high cost) or too aggressive (quality regressions for some tenants). This PR implements a tenant profile matcher that chooses a cost-aware defaults bundle (batching, prefill/caching hints, quantization profile preference) based on per-tenant telemetry signals, and a deterministic fallback chain for quant profiles to ensure graceful quality-first degradation. Motivation: reduce unit cost for conservative tenants while preserving output quality and providing predictable rollback behavior when telemetry indicates regressions.

What this PR changes: 1) pkg/econ/matcher.go: new matching engine that ingests a compact feature vector (median request tokens, 95th pct tail, burstiness, recent error-rate delta, embedding vs generation mix) and maps it to a named preset (e.g., "compact-latency-safe", "balanced-cost", "quality-first"). 2) configs/presets/tenant-presets.yaml: curated presets with explicit quantization fallback chains and batch/cache knobs. 3) telemetry/prefill_signals_ingest.py: lightweight transformer to compute tenant feature vectors and write to signal-store. 4) cmd/rwctl/profile-preview.go: CLI to preview which preset would be chosen for a tenant and to simulate fallback decisions given an observed degradation. 5) docs/tenant-profiles.md: doc + decision table and recommended rollout plan. 6) tests: unit + simulated workload integration test that replays sampled traces to verify fallback ordering and no silent regressions. 7) a feature flag (feature.tenant_profile_matcher) and migration notes to enable gradual rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Matcher algorithm + serialization format defined in code and docs - [x] Default presets added and reviewed by econ/ops - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan in docs - [x] Unit + integration tests, and a small bench comparing 95p latency and token-cost delta - [x] rwctl preview command and examples in docs - [x] Telemetry enrichment - [x] CI green (unit/integration/bench)

Linear/Jira: ENG-1421 covers the matcher implementation and tests; ENG-1422 covers presets and rollout. Support ticket SUP-9034 requested safer quant fallbacks for a high-cost tenant.

Notes on safety: The matcher returns a preset name only. All runtime controllers continue to validate that the selected quant profile is allowed per-tenant policy; if disallowed, the runtime will choose the next allowed profile from the fallback chain. The fallback chain prioritizes quality-preserving paths (e.g., int8->q4_0->q4_k_m) rather than immediate low-bit aggressive jumps.

Migration/rollout: Start with a small percentage (5%) of tenants behind feature flag plus rwctl dry-run preview reports. If telemetry shows >1% generation quality delta for any tenant, the runtime triggers an automatic opt-out and an alert to SRE.

Links: - RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1421/tenant-profile-matcher - Design doc: docs/tenant-profiles.md

review_comments: Maya Chen: Overall this looks good. Two items: please add a feature flag check in the matcher path (so we can toggle per-cluster), and confirm that fallback chain respects tenant deny-lists. Also can you add a small benchmark to ensure matcher latency is <1ms in the hot path?

Asha Patel (author): Added a feature flag gate and moved heavy serialization to an async precompute path. Benchmarks added under Makefile target 'bench-matcher' — median 0.6ms on dev machines. Registry consults tenant policies before finalizing selection.
Luca Romano: Suggest making the fallback chain prioritize 'no-quant-change' first (i.e., prefer batch/cache changes before quant if possible) — otherwise risk of unnecessary quant switching.
Asha Patel: Adjusted mapping to include 'prefers_cache_then_batch' ordering and updated docs with decision table. Added unit test that asserts fallback ordering in 4 scenarios.
Priya Singh: Accepted. Verified integration sim for three tenant traces; no regressions. Approving pending green CI.
CI Bot: All checks passed. Integration sim completed with <0.5% token-cost reduction and no regression in quality metrics in the simulated tenants.
